newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia puts 25 pct foreign investment limit on UES.
newsitem.headline: Russia puts 25 pct foreign investment limit on UES.

text.p: Russia's State Duma lower house of parliament passed a bill limiting foreign investors' holdings in the national power company Unified Energy System to 25 percent, a Duma official said on Wednesday.

"Foreign states, international organisations, foreign corporate bodies and Russian corporate bodies affiliated to them and foreign individuals can hold up to 25 percent of UES shares," said the bill, which amends a previous law.

The bill was passed in a second reading and the third reading will take place on Friday. To become law it will then need to be approved by the Federation Council upper house of parliament and signed by President Boris Yeltsin.

Alexei Golovkov, deputy head of the Duma's budget committee, told Reuters that the new amendment would not allow foreigners to get enough shares to veto decisions at shareholders' meetings, for instance when new share issues are being discussed.
"Let our people get richer, as UES shares are rising. The amendment's goal is that," he said.
UES shares rose on Wednesday to $0.2120 from $0.0915 on December 31.
During the second reading Golovkov proposed a complete ban on foreign shares in UES, but as foreigners already own 22.5 percent of the company the amendment could not be passed in his version.
The RAO Yedinaya Energeticheskaya Sistema Rossii (UES) charter says that a single shareholder cannot have more than one percent of shares without UES board agreement.

The state owns 52.5 percent of the company, of which 51 percent will be held by the government until December 31, 1998, although another law does not set a time limit on the state's majority shareholding.
